info:
  title: Inventory reservation events
  version: 1.0.0
  description: Inventory reservations made for orders awaiting fulfillment.
  contact:
    name: Demo domain maintainers
  license:
    name: Apache-2.0
defaultContentType: application/json
servers:
  kafka:
    host: kafka.example.invalid:9092
    protocol: kafka
    description: Client deployment supplies the Kafka broker; this contract does not
      provision it.
    bindings:
      kafka:
        schemaRegistryUrl: https://apicurio.apps.cluster-ggvsm.dyn.redhatworkshops.io/apis/registry/v3
        schemaRegistryVendor: apicurio
        bindingVersion: 0.5.0
channels:
  reservations:
    address: demo.inventory.reservations
    servers:
    - $ref: '#/servers/kafka'
    messages:
      reserved:
        $ref: '#/components/messages/InventoryReserved'
operations:
  receiveReservations:
    action: receive
    channel:
      $ref: '#/channels/reservations'
    messages:
    - $ref: '#/channels/reservations/messages/reserved'
components:
  schemas:
    CloudEventHeaders:
      type: object
      required:
      - ce_specversion
      - ce_id
      - ce_source
      - ce_type
      properties:
        ce_specversion:
          type: string
          const: '1.0'
        ce_id:
          type: string
        ce_source:
          type: string
        ce_type:
          type: string
  messages:
    InventoryReserved:
      name: InventoryReserved
      title: Inventory reserved for an order
      summary: Inventory reservation confirmed for fulfillment planning.
      contentType: application/json
      headers:
        $ref: '#/components/schemas/CloudEventHeaders'
      payload:
        schemaFormat: application/schema+json;version=draft-07
        schema:
          $schema: http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#
          title: InventoryReserved
          type: object
          required:
          - orderId
          - sku
          - quantity
          properties:
            orderId:
              type: string
            sku:
              type: string
            quantity:
              type: integer
              minimum: 1
            warehouseId:
              type: string
              description: Warehouse holding the reserved stock.
          additionalProperties: false
      examples:
      - name: ReservedStock
        headers:
          ce_specversion: '1.0'
          ce_id: reservation-001
          ce_source: /inventory
          ce_type: demo.inventory.reserved
        payload:
          orderId: order-1001
          sku: widget-blue
          quantity: 2
          warehouseId: chicago-01

      schemaFormat: application/vnd.apache.avro;version=1.9.0

        type: record

        namespace: io.github.contractfirstkafka.demo.orderfulfillment

          - {name: reason, type: string}

      schemaFormat: application/schema+json;version=draft-07

        $schema: http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#

        type: object
        required: [orderId, trackingId]
        properties:
          orderId: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Identifier'}
          trackingId: {type: string, minLength: 1}
        additionalProperties: false
    Identifier: {type: string, minLength: 1}
  messages:
    OrderAccepted:
      name: OrderAccepted
      contentType: application/avro
      headers: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/CloudEventHeaders'}
      payload: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/OrderAcceptedPayload'}

      examples:
        - name: accepted-order
          headers: {ce_specversion: '1.0', ce_id: event-001, ce_source: /orders, ce_type: demo.order.accepted}
          payload: {orderId: order-001, total: 49.95}
    OrderCancelled:
      name: OrderCancelled
      contentType: application/avro
      headers: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/CloudEventHeaders'}
      payload: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/OrderCancelledPayload'}
      bindings:
        kafka: {schemaIdLocation: header, bindingVersion: 0.5.0}
      examples:
        - name: cancelled-order
          headers: {ce_specversion: '1.0', ce_id: event-002, ce_source: /orders, ce_type: demo.order.cancelled}
          payload: {orderId: order-002, reason: customer-request}
    ShipmentDispatched:
      name: ShipmentDispatched
      headers: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/CloudEventHeaders'}
      payload: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/ShipmentPayload'}
      bindings:
        kafka: {schemaIdLocation: header, bindingVersion: 0.5.0}
      examples:
        - name: dispatched-shipment
          headers: {ce_specversion: '1.0', ce_id: event-003, ce_source: /shipments, ce_type: demo.shipment.dispatched}
          payload: {orderId: order-001, trackingId: tracking-001}

data.body:
# Demo

Order fulfillment architecture and independent event contracts.

This catalog documents independent API contracts. A contract service describes an
interface, not a deployed application or a verified producer/consumer.

## Architecture decisions

Contracts remain authoritative in their own Git repositories. Domain and System
relationships come from the existing Domain activation and System API references.

Add business concepts, cross-system processes, and architecture decisions here or
as additional native EventCatalog documentation pages. Generated resources are
build outputs and do not replace these authored pages.

## Fulfillment flow

Reserve inventory before arranging shipment. Order acceptance, stock reservation,
and shipment dispatch are separate business facts documented by independent
contracts. This architecture describes the intended process; it does not claim
that producers or consumers have been deployed.

## Agent discovery

The web UI and native MCP endpoint at `/docs/mcp` expose the same generated
architecture and authoritative contract snapshots. Agents can inspect schemas
and declared relationships without publishing contracts to a second destination.

Use it whenever the user wants to see or understand how something works or fits together, e.g. "show me how the Order Service works", "how does the Ordering domain fit together", "what does Payments talk to", or asks for a diagram, map or visual of something. Prefer it over drawing your own diagram. For domains and systems, pass detail "overview" for just the domains, systems and their relationships, or "full" (default) to include services, messages and channels. "schema" shows the schema of a message (event, command or query) or other resource: its properties, types, descriptions and which ones are required. Use it whenever the user wants to see or understand a schema or payload, e.g. "show me the schema for OrderCreated", "what fields does PlaceOrder have", "what does the OrderShipped payload look like". Clients that support MCP Apps show one viewer and switch it to each thing you show, so call this again to show the user something else. The result also contains what is shown (the diagram as Mermaid in mermaidCode, or the schema code) so you can understand it. When the client shows the viewer, do not redraw the diagram or print the whole schema again in your reply: explain it and point out what matters.
